title: Verifier-guided representation refinement: can persistent semantic structure be repaired from counterexamples without regressing verified behavior?
question: When a frozen representation fails a registered dynamic-validity test, can structured verifier counterexamples guide a bounded representation refinement process that reduces future behavioral violations while preserving previously verified invariants?
hypothesis: Targeted representation refinement driven by structured counterexamples will reduce dynamic-validity violations and recover or preserve task capability more effectively than leaving the representation frozen, while a no-regression gate will prevent repaired representations from silently invalidating previously verified behavioral constraints.

arms.name: frozen
arms.intervention: retain the initial VRS representation unchanged after counterexamples

arms.name: error_driven_refinement
arms.intervention: generate a revised representation proposal from the frozen representation plus structured verifier counterexamples; re-calibrate and re-validate before admission

arms.name: scalar_refinement_control
arms.intervention: apply the same counterexample-driven refinement budget to a one-dimensional scalar representation

arms.name: oracle_behavioral_repair
arms.intervention: diagnostic-only refinement using exhaustive future-behavior information unavailable to practical refinement

endpoints.name: dynamic_violation_rate_after_refinement
endpoints.role: primary — dynamic-validity violation rate after the fixed refinement budget, among representations satisfying the no-regression and capability gates
endpoints.description: Final violation rate over the fixed pre-generated dynamic test set after the registered number of refinement cycles.

endpoints.name: capability_retention
endpoints.role: secondary — exact task capability relative to the initial raw-state reference

endpoints.name: counterexample_resolution_rate
endpoints.role: secondary — proportion of previously observed verifier counterexamples no longer reproduced after refinement

endpoints.name: new_violation_rate
endpoints.role: secondary — violations introduced on previously unseen fixed validation cases

endpoints.name: verified_invariant_retention
endpoints.role: secondary — fraction of previously verified anchors/behavioral invariants still satisfied

endpoints.name: representation_drift
endpoints.role: secondary — geometric/version distance between successive representations

endpoints.name: refinement_cost
endpoints.role: secondary — semantic proposal/extraction calls, wall-clock, and downstream validation compute per refinement cycle

held_constant: initial representation proposal and calibration are identical across refinement arms
fixed training/evaluation structures, truth tables, pair sets, action schedules, verifier, exact executor, seeds, and capability definition
all counterexample cases are generated before representation refinement begins and are hashed
repair/refinement cannot observe hidden target identity or unexecuted future outcomes except through the registered structured verifier record
refinement budget is fixed at three proposal cycles
oracle_behavioral_repair is diagnostic-only and cannot win the practical primary endpoint
previously verified invariants are immutable admission constraints unless explicitly marked as a registered replacement
new validation cases are independent of the counterexamples used to drive refinement
all representation versions and proposal artifacts are persisted with content digests
representation construction and validation cost are separately reported

decision_rule.condition: The initial representation fails dynamic validity but all integrity gates pass.
decision_rule.licenses: representation failure is eligible for structured repair testing.
decision_rule.does_not_license: permission to change the representation until the result looks favorable.

decision_rule.condition: error_driven_refinement lowers dynamic_violation_rate_after_refinement, retains >=0.80 capability, and retains all previously verified invariants within the registered tolerance.
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence for verifier-guided representation repair on the registered workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: general representation self-improvement, asymptotic scaling, or universal LLM repair.

decision_rule.condition: refinement lowers old counterexamples but introduces new violations or loses verified invariants.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence of representation repair tradeoff/failure under the registered regime; the repaired version is not admitted as persistent verified structure.

decision_rule.condition: no refinement arm reduces the primary endpoint while passing capability and no-regression gates.
decision_rule.licenses: the registered repair process does not solve the representation failure.

forbidden_inputs: verifier-only future rows not present in the counterexample
refinement_protocol.proposal_freeze: Each proposed version is frozen before its own validation run. A validation result cannot modify the proposal that produced it.

no_regression.admission: A repaired representation is persistent/verified only if all registered invariants remain satisfied within tolerance.
no_regression.replacement: Changing an invariant definition requires a new experiment identifier rather than an outcome-dependent edit.

data_splits.repair_validation: fixed cases distinct from counterexample-driving cases
data_splits.final_test: hidden from refinement and representation repair
data_splits.target_disjointness: train/evaluation structures and complete truth tables are independently split

prior_art: Abstraction Agent, arXiv:2609.04303 — semantic feature synthesis with downstream solver evaluation and proposed solver-in-loop refinement
LLMs as Feature Engineers for Text-and-Tabular Prediction, arXiv:2609.21894 — separate proposal/extraction loop driven by explicit downstream errors
VERDI, arXiv:2608.09537 — counterexample/contradiction-guided diagnostic evolution and target-side validation
RefineICL, arXiv:2609.27679 — support-driven in-situ representation refinement without parameter updates
LOTUS, arXiv:2608.15509 — behavioral/bisimulation constraints for task representations
not_inherited: none of these establish verifier-guided persistent representation repair in TAC-OSM
none establish no-regression under continual representation updates
none establish selective operator execution after representation repair

nonclaims: no claim that every verifier counterexample has a representational fix
no claim that LLM repair is intrinsically superior to non-LLM optimization
no claim that representation drift toward a lower dynamic-violation rate is globally beneficial
no claim that repaired representations replace underlying evidence
